ideas.title: Stop Before The Ending
ideas.trend: Ads that show the first part of a story and stop, so viewers wonder what happens next (from a mobile game ad guide)
ideas.why_now: The only signal is this evergreen ad guide, which recommends video ads that show the opening chapters so users wonder how it goes on; it is a known practice, not a trend dated today.
ideas.mapping: The 'make them wonder' idea becomes a cliffhanger ending: the video stops with blocks still on the board and asks the viewer to finish it, so the gameplay itself is the unfinished story.
ideas.prompt: Concept: 'how does this end?' Make a 35-second ad on a medium-sized board with a narrow centre and 8 varied blocks, hard difficulty, normal tempo that slows down near the end. First move the yellow block aside, then the green and blue blocks leave one after another, then stop on a cliffhanger with two blocks left, a red one stuck behind an orange one. Hook: "How does this end?" End card line: "Your move." Leave out the replay.

ideas.title: Calm Puzzle, Busy Brain
ideas.trend: Mobile game ads that sell an emotion, from relaxation to mental stimulation (from a mobile game ad guide)
ideas.why_now: The same guide says game categories and their ads target feelings like relaxation and mental stimulation; this is general advice, not something trending today.
ideas.mapping: The relaxation-plus-brain-work feeling sets a calm tempo, a pastel theme, a spacious easy board and a clean win where the blocks all leave in a cascade.
ideas.prompt: Concept: a relaxing puzzle that still makes you think. Make a 30-second ad in a pastel theme on a small board with plenty of empty cells and 6 chunky blocks, easy difficulty and a calm tempo. No mistakes and one hesitation: the player picks a block up and puts it back. Then one move frees everything and they all leave one after another for a clean win. Hook: "Relax. Then think." White captions with a soft outline, no cursor.

skipped.trend: Simulation-game storyline ads with plots and characters
skipped.why: Color Block Jam has no characters or story, so only the 'leave them wondering' structure carries over.
